# FeaturePanel

Group: Layout. Import: `import { FeaturePanel } from 'lynn-ui';`

The large narrative walkthrough panel.
 Ported from wings-2026.html's `.walk-panel` family: a 24px-radius panel lit by two opposite-corner radial glows over the `card` fill, a gradient stripe along its top edge, then an uppercase pill, a heading, a body capped at 620px, and a row of actions.

## Usage

One panel per step of a walkthrough, and let the `actions` row be the hand-off - the first action defaults to `primary` and the rest to `secondary`, so a two-action panel needs no `variant` at all. `body` takes markup for the source's bold clauses, and anything richer (a step list, a figure, a nested `CodeBlock`) goes in `children`, which renders below the actions. `accentGradient` re-tints only the 2px top stripe.

## Don't

Don't try to put a custom control in `actions` - it is typed as `FeaturePanelAction` data, not nodes, precisely so every action is guaranteed to be a real `Button`; put anything else in `children`. And `badge` is always rendered `tone="lynn"`, so don't pass a `Badge` of your own expecting the tone to survive - pass the label text.

## Props

- `badge?: ReactNode` - Uppercase pill above the heading.
- `heading: ReactNode`
- `body?: ReactNode` - Narrative body. Pass markup to keep the source's bold clauses.
- `actions?: FeaturePanelAction[]` - The action row. Taken as data rather than as nodes so every action is guaranteed to be a real `Button` - the panel's whole job is to be the place a walkthrough hands the reader off from.
- `accentGradient?: string` - Any CSS gradient for the 2px top stripe. Defaults to the source's real `blue -> indigo -> emerald` sweep.
- `id?: string` - Anchor id, so a DocRail section link can jump to this panel.
- `children?: ReactNode` - Extra content below the actions - a step list, a note, a figure.
- `className?: string`
- `style?: CSSProperties`
